register.rule: daily change in the Yes price of 'Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by December 31?' read at 12:00 UTC (the last hourly point at or before 12:00:00 UTC; hourly points are stamped seconds after the hour, so in practice the 11:00 UTC sample) vs next-day Brent (BZ=F) log return, controlling for Brent's own same-day log return: OLS of the next-day return on [change, same-day return] with an intercept, Newey-West t with 5 lags; the slope and t are those of the change; the pass mark reads the chance by luck: the share of runs, the real one and every circular shift of the next-day return against the change by 5 to n - 5 days, whose robust (HC0) t-statistic of the change is at least as large in size, both series first taken as residuals on [1, same-day return]
register.question: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by December 31?
register.pass_mark: slope < 0 and chance by luck (p_shift) < 0.05 over at least 60 trading days after 2026-10-29
register.calendar: the asset's own trading days (dates with a Brent close in the World file)
register.why: with no link at all (the Indian moves shuffled, moved 60 or 120 days, or given random signs while keeping their size), a t-statistic beyond 2 turned up in 11.6% to 15.5% of the co-movement table's rows, where about 5% is expected, while the chance by luck fell under 5% in 4.0% to 5.7% of them; neither version had scored a day when this one was written down
